newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes fall with NYMEX, markets dead.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes fall with NYMEX, markets dead.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices fell on Friday tracking a downward correction on NYMEX, though activity was seriously tempered by an industry function in the Sierra Nevada mountains northeast of San Francisco.
"There's really nothing going on," said a trader, one of the few who was not attending the 12th Annual West Coast Crude Oil Conference in Lake Tahoe on Thursday and Friday.

March West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell sharply on Friday, but due largely to correcting heating oil futures prices, which rallied earlier in the week on cold weather in the Northeast, where U.S. home heat oil use is concentrated.
The Alaskan crude market held steady after a deal got done on Wednesday at $1.45 under March, the same price as a deal done on January 17.

Heavy crude markets were also quiet because of the absense of players. But earlier this week, heavy became a stronger alternative to ANS after 40,000 barrels came into the market following a force majeure by Tosco.
With heavy crude prices expected to drop below their current $17.25 range, refiners were looking at ways to run heavies instead of light grades.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
